title: Transient fill of an empty part-full conduit in a closed system, scored at rest
registrationStatus: REGISTERED 12 Nov 2026: draft 3 approved by technical review (decision of 12 Nov 2026, filed as reviews/approval-2026-11-12.md), with four documentation clarifications made at approval (definitionRevisions, draft 3a). Criteria hashed as criteriaRevisions[0]. Run as the first PVM2 experiment.
process: a dry conduit filling from one end and coming to rest: the wetting front, link storage during the transition from dry to part full, storage at intermediate junctions, closed-system volume
relatedSpecs: PV-C1: its criteria are carried here (criteriaNotes); its frozen results (results/2026-11-11T18-57-58-574Z) are not rerun. Not a run dependency (definition revision at approval: dependsOn removed so that run.mjs --only PV-TF1 runs PV-TF1 and nothing else)
equations: continuity of the closed system: V(t) = V0 + integral of the declared inflow from 0 to t (no outflow: the sealing weir must never flow)

at rest (still water): one level h everywhere; V_rest = sum_i A_i h + L A_circle(h) + 0 (junctions have no plan area in the reference) for a horizontal conduit at invert 0 (references/volume.mjs equilibriumDepth)
SWMM solves the dynamic-wave Saint-Venant equations; only the at-rest state has an exact reference here
referenceAssumptions: R1 still water at rest: one free-surface level in both tanks, every junction and every conduit; no residual motion beyond the rest definition (criteria.rest*)
R2 the tanks are prismatic, 20 m^2, invert 0 (SWMM FUNCTIONAL 0 0 20; checked by the node-volume row)
R3 the conduit is horizontal at invert 0 end to end; its at-rest volume is L A_circle(h), exact for a level surface in a prismatic horizontal conduit

R4 junctions have zero plan area and zero volume (manholes are not modelled as storage). This matches SWMM's own definition: a junction's volume is identically 0 (node.c: fullVolume 0 at read, node_initState fullVolume = node_getVolume(fullDepth) = 0, so node_getVolume returns 0). It is checked by a scored row, not assumed silently
R5 the declared inflow series is the only source; SWMM applies it to within about 2e-4 (FINDINGS.md F1 evidence; reported row)
R6 the reference is computed from the declared inputs only (geometry, series); no SWMM output enters it
initialConditions: everything dry: T1, T2, every junction and every conduit at depth 0
boundaryConditions: declared inflow into T1: a trapezoid hydrograph 0 -> 0.1 m^3/s over 60 s, held to 1800 s, 0.1 -> 0 over 60 s (integral exactly 180.0 m^3); no other inflow; the only outfall is behind a weir whose crest is above every reachable level (SWMM refuses a network with no outfall, ERROR 145; same device as PV-C1)
geometry: T1 and T2: prismatic storage, 20 m^2 each, 3 m deep, invert 0. Conduit: circular D 1.0 m, total length 400 m, n 0.013, horizontal (both ends at invert 0, no offsets), cut into N equal segments joined by N - 1 junctions at invert 0, max depth 3 m. Sealing weir W0: T2 -> OUT, crest 2.5 m

segments.unit: - (each scored separately; N = 1 has no intermediate junction)

referenceLevel.unit: m (equilibriumDepth, computed before any run; conduit 159.73 m^3 = 88.7 % of the system)

sampleS.unit: s (raw time series); the rest-window flow and flux conditions are evaluated at every routing step

guardDepthFrac.unit: - of D: any node depth at or above this, at any routing step, makes the case Invalid setup (keeps the pipe away from the crown and from finding F1)

conduitGuardDepthFrac.unit: - of D (draft 3): any conduit segment's LINK_DEPTH at or above this, at any routing step of the whole run, makes the case Invalid setup for scoring; decided from the full per-step series, never from the final or resting state (fullConduitGuard)

minSurfArea.unit: m^2 (SWMM default, as lib/swmm-run.mjs; applies to every node, binds only at junctions here: the tanks' own 20 m^2 exceeds it)

solver: SWMM 5.2.4 production wasm (vendor/swmm-wasm) through lib/swmm-run.mjs: CMS, DYNWAVE, EXTRAN surcharge, INERTIAL_DAMPING PARTIAL, NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED BOTH, MIN_SLOPE 0, MIN_SURFAREA 1.167, fixed 1 s step, MAX_TRIALS 8, HEAD_TOLERANCE 0.0015. Hand-written .inp, no FloodSim translation in the loop. Production routing settings are not changed

reference.sources: geometry of a circular segment (references/geometry.mjs area, cross-checked by quadrature in refs.test.mjs); the declared inflow series; still-water hydrostatics
reference.independence: the reference uses only the declared inputs and assumptions R1-R6; no SWMM quantity enters it; the at-rest state does not depend on how the transient was solved
reference.crossCheck: equilibriumDepth by bisection on the exact volume function; the circle area by quadrature (refs.test.mjs, existing)

whySWMMCanStoreOrLoseWaterAtAJunction: J1 node volume: SWMM's junction volume is identically 0 (R4). Scored row: the sum of NODE_VOLUME over the N - 1 junctions, at every sample, must be 0 (criteria.junctionVolumeAbsM3). If it is not 0, the books are reported with and without it, and R4 is falsified.

J2 minimum surface area: a junction's depth changes by dV / max(surface area, MIN_SURFAREA) (dynwave.c line 670), the surface area being half of each joined conduit's surface. While a junction's conduits are nearly dry their area is below MIN_SURFAREA, so depth moves as if 1.167 m^2 of storage were there; that storage has no volume (J1). This is not a stored volume and cannot be read from the API; it can only show as an at-rest closure error. A priori bound on its size, from geometry only: (N - 1) x 1.167 m^2 x 0.507 m = 0 (N 1), 1.8 m^3 (N 4), 8.9 m^3 (N 16), 18.3 m^3 (N 32), against a criterion of 0.18 m^3: the test can see it at every N >= 4 if it acts.

J3 link storage carried by the end nodes: SWMM keeps a conduit's storage implicitly, through half of its surface area at each end node, and the conduit's own volume is L x A(mid depth) (dwflow.c line 291). This is the mechanism of predictions P2a (all N, including N 1).
junctionStorage.diagnosticToSeparateJ2: MIN_SURFAREA 0.1 m^2 (bound 1.6 m^3 at N 32): declared now, unscored

fullConduitGuard.why: F1 (crown cutoff) acts on the depths SWMM uses inside a conduit, not only on node depths; the guard must be decided on the conduit's own depth state at every routing step
checks: G-node (retained from draft 2): at every routing step, every node (T1, T2, every junction): NODE_DEPTH (API code 303) / D < 0.9

G-node endpoint coverage (clarification at approval): the guard is applied per conduit segment to BOTH of its endpoint nodes, read from the API at run time (LINK_NODE1 401 and LINK_NODE2 402), not from a list written by hand: C1 has T1 and J1 (T1 and T2 when N = 1), Ck has J(k-1) and Jk, CN has J(N-1) and T2. The downstream terminal endpoint of the conduit chain is T2, a storage node. No conduit segment has an outfall as an endpoint in this geometry: the outfall OUT is joined only to the sealing weir W0 (T2 -> OUT). OUT's NODE_DEPTH is checked at every step as well, so every node of the network, the outfall included, is covered, and if any conduit endpoint read from the API were an outfall it would be checked like any other endpoint
G-link (new): at every routing step of the whole run, every conduit segment C1..CN: LINK_DEPTH (API code 411) / LINK_FULLDEPTH (API code 405; must read 1.0 m, else Invalid setup) < 0.9
fullConduitGuard.decision: either check reaching >= 0.9 at any routing step => Invalid setup for scoring (no closure or level row is scored for that N). Decided from the complete per-step series
fullConduitGuard.recorded: for each check and each N: the maximum ratio, the node or conduit segment where it occurs, the routing step index and simulated time (s), and the depth (m); also the per-segment maximum LINK_DEPTH / D over the run
fullConduitGuard.whatSWMMHoldsAsConduitDepth: SWMM has no depth profile along a conduit. Its dynamic-wave update (dwflow.c lines 107-128 and 150) forms two end depths y1 = h1 - z1 and y2 = h2 - z2 from the end nodes' heads and the conduit invert (node invert + offset), floored at FUDGE and, under EXTRAN, capped at full depth; then yMid = (y1 + y2) / 2. Only yMid is stored for the link: Link.newDepth = MIN(yMid, yFull) (dwflow.c line 287), which is what LINK_DEPTH returns (swmm5.c, swmm_LINK_DEPTH). y1 and y2 are local to the routine and not exposed by any getter; Conduit.fullState (the full/part-full flag) is stored but not exposed either. In PV-TF1's geometry (every offset 0) the end-depth substitutions of findSurfArea for UP_CRITICAL / DN_CRITICAL cannot occur (getFlowClass assigns them only when an offset is > 0, dwflow.c lines 297-360), so y1 and y2 are exactly the end nodes' depths (capped, floored) or FUDGE when dry.
fullConduitGuard.linkDepthIsAMidpointObservation: clarification at approval: LINK_DEPTH is a recorded midpoint observation, SWMM's own computed mean of its two end depths (yMid, capped at full depth) as it stands at the end of each routing step. It is not an independent measurement of the conduit's depth profile: SWMM has no profile, and LINK_DEPTH contains no information beyond the two end depths it is formed from. G-link and the conduit water-surface check observe this recorded value; neither is evidence about the depth at any other point along the conduit
fullConduitGuard.coverage: G-link covers the only conduit depth SWMM stores (yMid). The end depths y1 and y2 at which the crown cutoff can also act (getWidth on y1, y2 and yMid) are not link variables; in this geometry they equal the end nodes' depths by SWMM's own construction, so they are covered by G-node. This is stated here as a limitation, not assumed: see limitations and the unresolved objection in reviews/resolution-I1.md

restHydraulicEquilibrium.why: reference R1 assumes one level everywhere; equal stable tank levels and low flows do not establish that the junctions and conduits are at that level
restHydraulicEquilibrium.commonDatum: SWMM's elevation datum: every elevation below is an absolute water-surface elevation (m), never a raw depth
restHydraulicEquilibrium.tankWSE: at each routing step, mean of NODE_HEAD (304) of T1 and T2 (the existing restLevelDiffM condition keeps them within 1 mm of each other)
restHydraulicEquilibrium.junctionWSE: NODE_HEAD (304) of every intermediate junction J1..J(N-1) (SWMM: newDepth + invertElev)
restHydraulicEquilibrium.conduitWSE: for every conduit segment: z_mid + LINK_DEPTH (411), with z_mid = (NODE_ELEV(301) of node1 + offset1 + NODE_ELEV(301) of node2 + offset2) / 2 and both offsets declared 0. This is the water surface of SWMM's only stored conduit depth (yMid). If LINK_DEPTH equals LINK_FULLDEPTH the cap binds, the surface is not defined, and the rest condition is not met
restHydraulicEquilibrium.conduitWseInvertAssumption: clarification at approval: the conduit water-surface elevation uses the horizontal, zero-offset invert assumption: the conduit's invert is taken to be the same elevation (0 m) at both ends and at its midpoint, so that z_mid is the elevation under the recorded mid-depth. This holds only under hardValidityConditions; on a sloped conduit or one with an offset, z_mid + LINK_DEPTH would not be the water surface at any defined point, and the check would not be valid
restHydraulicEquilibrium.condition: at every routing step of the rest window: |junctionWSE - tankWSE| <= restInternalWseAbsM for every junction and |conduitWSE - tankWSE| <= restInternalWseAbsM for every segment; the existing restSegmentFlowAbsM3s and sealing-weir conditions are retained
restHydraulicEquilibrium.decision: any violation at any step of the rest window => the at-rest rows are Insufficient reference data (not a pass, not a fail)
restHydraulicEquilibrium.recorded: for each N: the maximum internal deviation, its location (junction or conduit id), the routing step index and simulated time; separately for junctions and conduits
restHydraulicEquilibrium.note: in this horizontal zero-offset geometry SWMM's conduit surface is by construction the mean of its two end nodes' heads, so the conduit check follows from the junction and tank checks; it is kept because that equality is a property of the SWMM scheme, which the check should observe rather than assume

hardValidityConditions.statement: clarification at approval: zero offsets and a horizontal conduit are HARD validity conditions. The end-depth equivalence on which the full-conduit guard relies (fullConduitGuard.whatSWMMHoldsAsConduitDepth: no UP_CRITICAL or DN_CRITICAL substitution) and the conduit water-surface calculation (restHydraulicEquilibrium.conduitWseInvertAssumption) are valid only under them. Any deviation invalidates the experiment
checkedAtRunTime: V1 both offset fields of every conduit segment (inlet offset and outlet offset in [CONDUITS]) are 0 in the .inp text as opened by SWMM (parsed back from the written file; SWMM's API has no offset getter)
V2 NODE_ELEV (301) of every node is 0 m (both endpoints of every segment, the tanks, the junctions, the outfall)

V3 every conduit segment is level as SWMM itself sees it. SWMM never stores a slope of 0: conduit_getSlope (link.c lines 1257-1299) replaces an end-invert drop below MIN_DELTA_Z (0.001 ft) by 0.001 ft and writes WARNING 04 (minimum elevation drop used). So V3 requires both: LINK_SLOPE (404) equal to that nominal value, 0.001 / sqrt(L_ft^2 - 0.001^2) (3.048e-6 at 100 m), to 1e-12 relative; and the report's WARNING 04 line for that conduit. Any other slope means SWMM saw a real elevation drop. Geometric horizontality itself is V1 + V2 (end inverts and offsets all 0). The nominal slope is SWMM's, used in its normal-flow limit (link.c line 1244) and a surcharge test (dynwave.c line 374); it is part of the registered configuration (NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED BOTH), not a deviation, and it does not enter the at-rest reference or the water-surface calculation
V4 LINK_LENGTH (403) of every segment is 400 / N m and their sum 400 m; LINK_FULLDEPTH (405) of every segment is 1.0 m

tolerance: exact (0) for V1 and V2; 1e-12 relative for V3; 1e-9 m for V4 (floating-point representation of the declared values: SWMM converts metres to its internal feet and back, so LINK_FULLDEPTH reads 0.9999999999999999)
hardValidityConditions.decision: any deviation in any case makes every row of that case Invalid setup, and the experiment as a whole is reported as invalid; it is not repaired and re-run under the same registration

stepping: both checks, and the rest-window flow and flux conditions, are evaluated at every routing step through SWMM.stepTo's per-step callback (src/swmm.js: one swmm_step call per callback; swmm5.c execRouting runs exactly one routing_execute per swmm_step, and the getters read the state at the end of that step). With a fixed 1 s step the run has durationS / routingStepS = 43200 steps; the step count and each step's length are recorded, and a count or length that differs makes the case Invalid setup rather than leaving steps unchecked. The run's final routing step is reported by swmm_step with an elapsed time of 0 (swmm5.c lines 446-449: the run has reached its duration); src/swmm.js stepTo would drop it, so the module calls swmm_step itself, keeps that step, and takes its end time from SWMM's own rule (execRouting: RouteStep, cut so the duration is not exceeded); this is flagged in the result (stepping.finalStepByRule). SWMM's duration is floor(days x 86400) s (project.c line 165); 43200 s is exactly 0.5 day, so 43200 steps are expected
rawOutput: every routing step (clarification at approval: all per-step output is preserved, not only 60 s samples), for every case including the declared diagnostics: the step length; for every node (tanks, junctions, outfall) NODE_DEPTH, NODE_HEAD, NODE_VOLUME, NODE_LATFLOW; for every conduit segment LINK_DEPTH, LINK_FLOW, LINK_VELOCITY; the sealing weir's LINK_FLOW. Saved unreduced as little-endian Float64, one row per step, gzip-compressed, in results/<run-id>/PV-TF1-raw-<case>.f64.gz, with a JSON header (PV-TF1-raw-<case>.json: the column names, units, row count, the .inp text as opened, the spec SHA-256, the SWMM version and wasm SHA-256). The 60 s series is a subset of it; the run's git commit and diff hash are in MANIFEST.json
outputs: SCORED, at rest, per N: volume closure: tanks (A d) + conduit L A(h) + junction NODE_VOLUME, against V0 + 180.0 m^3
SCORED, at rest, per N: the common level against referenceLevel
SCORED, per N: junction volume, sum over junctions, largest sample (R4, J1)
SCORED, per N: boundary flux over the sealing weir: largest absolute flow at any routing step of the whole run, largest within the rest window, and its integral over the run
SCORED, per N: SWMM's node volume against A d for each tank (internal consistency, as PV-C1)

VALIDITY, per N (decide whether the rows above are scored; not scored themselves): fullConduitGuard maxima (node and conduit, with location, step, time, depth, depth / D); restHydraulicEquilibrium maximum internal deviation (with location, step, time); routing step count

REPORTED, NOT SCORED: SWMM's flow-routing continuity error; the applied inflow (sum NODE_LATFLOW dt) against 180.0; the closure in motion at every sample (DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, see transientStatement); maximum node depth / D; each rest condition's margin; the closure's dependence on N
transientStatement: The closure in motion is a diagnostic only. During the transient the conduit's water surface is not level, its volume has no independent reference here (finding F4), and any in-motion closure figure uses SWMM's own depth representation. A transient discrepancy that disappears before rest does not establish that the transient was correct: the scored rows test the end state only. No statement about the transient's correctness is made from this test.
criteriaNotes: closureRel, equilibriumAbsM, restWindowS, restLevelDiffM, sealFluxAbs, nodeVolumeRel are PV-C1's, unchanged: 0.1 % of the at-rest system volume (= 0.113 % of the conduit's own volume; a component error cannot hide in a large system); known noise in these books is about 2e-4 (inflow interpolation, F1 evidence) and 1e-4 of the conduit volume (tabulated circle geometry, F4 evidence), about 5 times below the criterion. Rest (draft 2): over the last restWindowS of the run, at every sample both tank levels within restLevelDiffM of each other, each level's change over the window within restLevelDriftM, AND at every routing step every conduit segment's |Q| <= restSegmentFlowAbsM3s, AND the sealing weir's flow 0 at every step. 5e-6 m^3/s is the flow that would move 1 mm of one tank (20 m^2) in the hour of the window; held for the whole window it moves at most 0.018 m^3, a tenth of the closure criterion, so residual motion cannot decide a pass or a fail. Draft 3 adds a fourth rest condition: at every routing step of the window, every intermediate junction's and every conduit segment's water-surface elevation within restInternalWseAbsM (1 mm, the same tolerance as the tank-level condition) of the common tank water-surface elevation, compared in SWMM's elevation datum (restHydraulicEquilibrium); this establishes reference R1 (one level everywhere) rather than assuming it from the tanks. If any rest condition fails, the at-rest rows are Insufficient reference data (not a pass, not a fail) and a longer duration would need a definition revision. junctionVolumeAbsM3 1e-9: SWMM defines the volume as identically 0 (R4), so any non-round-off value falsifies R4. The criteria were chosen before any closed-system fill was run; T2-C's open-system evidence (FINDINGS.md F3) exists and informs the predictions only.

proposedCriteriaHistory.why: specification defects identified by review 5 (resolution-5.md items a, c, d): (1) rest was defined by tank levels only, so a conduit still exchanging water between the tanks with equal levels would have counted as at rest: added restSegmentFlowAbsM3s (every segment, every step) and made the level drift explicit (restLevelDriftM, the PV-C1 'level change within 1 mm over the last hour' rule, previously folded into restLevelDiffM); (2) the boundary flux was a largest sample at 60 s: now every routing step, the whole run and the rest window separately, plus its integral; (3) junction storage was not accounted: added the junction-volume row (junctionVolumeAbsM3). Every change adds a condition; none removes or widens one. Not hashed: hashing happens only at approval, as criteriaRevisions[0]

technical review I1, blocking objection 2 (resolution-I1.md): the rest definition did not establish the uniform hydraulic state assumed by R1; added restInternalWseAbsM (every junction and conduit segment, every step of the window, common datum). Blocking objection 1 adds a validity guard (parameters.conduitGuardDepthFrac, fullConduitGuard), not a criterion. Adds conditions only; closureRel, equilibriumAbsM, restWindowS, restLevelDiffM, restLevelDriftM, restSegmentFlowAbsM3s, sealFluxAbs, junctionVolumeAbsM3, nodeVolumeRel unchanged. Not hashed

conservation: closed system: the declared inflow is the only source, the sealing weir the only possible sink (scored zero, every step)
resolution: N = 1, 4, 16, 32 segments (12.5 m minimum); fixed 1 s routing step; diagnostic only: 0.5 s
predictions: P1 (open outfall): if T2-C came from its open outfall (outflow leaving before the barrel filled), the closed fill closes inside the criterion at every N.
P2a (link storage through end-node areas, J3): a fixed at-rest closure error of T2-C's sign (books above V0 + inflow), present at N = 1 and falling as N rises (T2-C's segmentation trend).
P2b (junction minimum surface area, J2): no error at N = 1 (no junction); an error that grows with N - 1, bounded by the J2 bound, and shrinking under the MIN_SURFAREA 0.1 m^2 diagnostic.
P3 (F1): no crown-cutoff loss: the guard keeps every node depth below 0.9 D.
None of P1, P2a, P2b is a pass condition; the rows are scored only against the criteria.

outcomeInterpretation.outcome: closes inside the criterion at every N, at rest
outcomeInterpretation.limitedTo: the end state of this closed horizontal fill; says nothing about the transient (transientStatement), about sloped conduits (PV-TF2), about the crown (PV-TF4), or about T2-C's open-system result, which stays Failed

outcomeInterpretation.outcome: error at N = 1, falling with N
outcomeInterpretation.limitedTo: a fill-time storage error in SWMM's representation for this geometry; its size at other diameters, lengths and tank areas is not established; B6-C's mechanism becomes a hypothesis to test, not a conclusion

outcomeInterpretation.outcome: no error at N = 1, error growing with N, reduced by MIN_SURFAREA 0.1
outcomeInterpretation.limitedTo: junction minimum surface area as one cause in this configuration; production's MIN_SURFAREA is not changed and its effect on production networks is not established

outcomeInterpretation.outcome: error at N = 1 and a non-monotone or sign-changing trend in N
outcomeInterpretation.supports: both P2a and P2b acting, possibly opposed (cf. F3's unexplained Q 0.5 sign change)
outcomeInterpretation.limitedTo: no attribution of shares; reported as observed; F3's Q 0.5 behaviour stays unexplained unless a separate registered test isolates it
Insufficient reference data; no conclusion about any prediction

outcomeInterpretation.outcome: guard trips or the sealing weir flows
outcomeInterpretation.limitedTo: Invalid setup; a geometry revision (not a criteria change) would be needed
the books are reported both ways; the closure rows stand as computed; the reference assumption is revised by a dated revision before any re-run

diagnostics: unscored, declared now: routing step 0.5 s; MIN_SURFAREA 0.1 m^2 (separates P2b); INERTIAL_DAMPING NONE (relation to finding F2); the instrumented build's conduit volume (getter 420) per segment, as a decomposition only (agreement with production shown on B1 only: an equality check of this case's node depths between the two builds precedes any use)

failureClasses.accounting: at-rest closure outside the criterion; junction volume not 0; sealing weir flow not 0
failureClasses.numerical: the closure or the level depends on N or on the step beyond the criterion
failureClasses.invalidSetup: a hard validity condition not met (hardValidityConditions V1-V4: an offset not 0, a node invert not 0, a slope not 0, a length or full depth not as declared), guard tripped (a node depth >= 0.9 D, or a conduit segment's LINK_DEPTH >= 0.9 D, at any routing step), the sealing weir flowed, LINK_FULLDEPTH not 1.0 m, or the routing step count or length not as declared
failureClasses.insufficientReference: any rest condition not met by the end of the run, including an internal water-surface deviation above 1 mm at any step of the rest window

assumptions: the API reads (NODE_DEPTH, NODE_VOLUME, NODE_LATFLOW, LINK_FLOW) are SWMM's state at the end of each routing step
limitations: scores only the end state: a transient error that undoes itself before rest is not seen, and its absence at rest does not establish transient correctness (transientStatement)
the minimum-surface-area mechanism (J2) is not observable directly through the production API; it is inferred from the N trend and the MIN_SURFAREA diagnostic

the conduit guard reads LINK_DEPTH, which is SWMM's mid-depth yMid capped at full depth: the only depth SWMM stores for a conduit. SWMM's conduit end depths y1, y2 and its full-state flag are not exposed by the production API; in this zero-offset geometry they equal the end nodes' depths by SWMM's construction and are covered by the node guard (fullConduitGuard.coverage). Exposing them would need read-only getters in the instrumented build, which is not done (resolution-I1.md)
the conduit water-surface check observes SWMM's single stored conduit depth (yMid); SWMM has no other water surface inside a conduit to check
LINK_DEPTH is a recorded midpoint observation (yMid), not an independent measurement of the conduit depth profile (fullConduitGuard.linkDepthIsAMidpointObservation)

the conduit water-surface elevation uses the horizontal, zero-offset invert assumption (restHydraulicEquilibrium.conduitWseInvertAssumption); zero offsets and a horizontal conduit are hard validity conditions (hardValidityConditions)
horizontal conduit only: a sloped conduit at rest has a varying depth and SWMM represents it by one mid-depth area (that is PV-TF2)
part full only: the crown transition and finding F1 are PV-TF4
one diameter, one roughness, one inflow rate, one tank size; one SWMM build

relationToFindings.F1: excluded by the guard (P3); not tested here; its SLOT question stays open
relationToFindings.F2: PARTIAL kept as registered; NONE only as a diagnostic; no criterion absorbs it
relationToFindings.F3: tested directly (P1, P2a, P2b); its registered T2-C rows stay Failed whatever the outcome; the Q 0.5 sign change stays open
relationToFindings.F4: not resolved: the in-motion closure is diagnostic only
relationToFindings.F5: addressed for this configuration: a declared net inflow into a closed system
relationToFindings.B6-C: a P2a or P2b outcome makes its mechanism a testable hypothesis; it is not resolved here

validRange: a horizontal circular conduit filled from dry to at most 0.9 D under dynamic-wave routing, closed system, ends at prismatic storage
scoring: automated, per N; status counts by error type; never a single pass percentage

criteriaRevisions.why: registration: draft 3 approved by the technical review decision of 12 Nov 2026 (milestone2/reviews/approval-2026-11-12.md), after technical review I1 (review-I1-2026-11-12.md, resolution-I1.md) and review 5; criteria as criteria draft 3 in proposedCriteriaHistory, unchanged at approval; hashed before any full-duration run of PV-TF1

definitionRevisions.why: review 5 items a-e: junction storage accounted (junctionStorage, R4, junction-volume row); every junction's depth and volume kept in the raw output; rest defined by tank levels plus a per-segment low-flow condition; boundary flux at every step, whole run and rest window; transientStatement added; predictions split into P2a/P2b with an outcome-interpretation table. Pre-registration: nothing hashed or run

technical review I1 blocking objections: (1) fullConduitGuard: a per-step guard on every conduit segment's LINK_DEPTH added beside the retained node guard, decided from the full series, with maximum, location, step and ratio recorded; (2) restHydraulicEquilibrium: every junction's and conduit segment's water-surface elevation within 1 mm of the common tank water surface at every step of the rest window, in SWMM's datum, violation => Insufficient reference data, maximum deviation, location and step recorded; stepping made explicit. documentation clarifications required by the technical review decision approving draft 3 (reviews/approval-2026-11-12.md), made before hashing: (1) G-node checks both endpoint nodes of every conduit segment, read from LINK_NODE1/LINK_NODE2; the chain's terminal endpoints are T1 and T2 (storage), no conduit has an outfall endpoint, and the outfall OUT is checked as well; (2) zero offsets and a horizontal conduit are hard validity conditions, checked at run time (hardValidityConditions V1-V4), any deviation invalidates the experiment; V3 states how SWMM represents a level conduit (it never stores slope 0 but a nominal 0.001 ft drop, with WARNING 04), found in a 300 s smoke test of the module before hashing (no at-rest result was produced or seen), so that the check tests horizontality as SWMM sees it rather than failing every case by construction; (3) LINK_DEPTH is a recorded midpoint observation, not an independent measurement of the depth profile; (4) the conduit water-surface calculation uses the horizontal, zero-offset invert assumption.
